subsystems.name: Quantum photon source payload
subsystems.role: produces the faint pulses of light that carry the key — either entangled photon pairs or weak laser pulses.

subsystems.name: Optical terminal
subsystems.role: aims that light at a ground telescope through a moving, turbulent atmosphere.

subsystems.name: Ground receiving station
subsystems.role: collects single photons and separates them from daylight.
parts: single-photon detectors (superconducting nanowire or avalanche diodes)

subsystems.name: Timing and classical channel
subsystems.role: marks which pulse is which and carries the public conversation needed to turn detections into a key.

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: stores keys and delivers them to users.

subsystems.name: Satellite bus
subsystems.role: keeps the payload powered, cold and pointing correctly.

buildSteps.title: Design the link budget
buildSteps.detail: Work out how many photons survive the trip: atmospheric loss, diffraction spreading over hundreds to thousands of kilometres, and telescope gains. This decides the orbit, the aperture sizes and the key rate.

buildSteps.title: Build and test the photon source
buildSteps.detail: A non-linear crystal is pumped by a laser to emit entangled pairs. On the bench, the team measures entanglement fidelity and count rate before anything is flight-qualified.

buildSteps.title: Space-qualify the optics
buildSteps.detail: The payload is shaken, baked in vacuum and cycled between hot and cold to prove the alignment of micrometre-scale optics survives launch and orbit.

buildSteps.title: Assemble payload and bus
buildSteps.detail: The optical bench is bolted into the satellite, wired to power and telemetry, and the telescope is aligned to the spacecraft axes.

buildSteps.title: Launch and commission
buildSteps.detail: After orbit insertion the payload is switched on, its pointing calibrated, and the telescope boresighted against known stars.

buildSteps.title: Acquire the ground link
buildSteps.detail: During a pass, the satellite finds the ground station's beacon, the station finds the satellite's downlink, and both steer to hold the link while the pair moves at kilometres per second.

buildSteps.title: Run the key exchange
buildSteps.detail: Photons are sent one at a time. The ground station records detections; over the public channel the two sides compare which pulses arrived, discard the rest, correct errors and compress what remains so any eavesdropping is squeezed out.

buildSteps.title: Distribute and relay keys
buildSteps.detail: Finished keys are stored and handed to users, or relayed through trusted ground nodes to link two cities that never see the satellite at once.

prerequisites.why: both are routine in laboratories and available commercially; the challenge is making them robust and fast enough in orbit.
satellite-to-ground and satellite-to-satellite optical links have been demonstrated, proving the pointing and acquisition problem is solvable.
a handful of missions have flown quantum sources and detectors, but long-lifetime, high-rate instruments are not yet off-the-shelf.
without them, entanglement cannot be stored or swapped, so long chains of links cannot be joined into a genuine end-to-end quantum network.

prerequisites.tech: Interoperable key-delivery standards and certified hardware
prerequisites.why: users need keys that plug into ordinary encryption equipment, with device behaviour they can trust.

pathway.milestone: low-Earth-orbit demonstrations such as China's Micius satellite, launched in 2016, which distributed entangled photons and keys to ground stations over more than 1,000 km
pathway.unlocks: proof that quantum signals survive a satellite link.

pathway.milestone: dedicated, higher-rate quantum satellites serving several ground stations per pass
pathway.unlocks: key delivery at rates and duty cycles useful to banks, utilities and governments.

pathway.milestone: constellations of satellites plus trusted ground nodes
pathway.unlocks: continent-scale key distribution, though with the caveat that intermediate nodes must be trusted.

pathway.milestone: satellite links joined by quantum repeaters and memories
pathway.unlocks: entanglement shared between distant users, removing trust assumptions and pointing towards a quantum internet. Note this carries keys, not data — the payload traffic still travels over ordinary channels.
